name: Ancient Hebrew (Biblical Hebrew)

ancestors.notes: Canaanite (Northwest Semitic), a branch of Central Semitic; ancestor of the whole Hebrew lineage, matching he.json's own placement.
Phoenician/Canaanite areal contact; the Hebrew and Phoenician consonant inventories and the paleo-Hebrew script both descend from the same Canaanite alphabetic tradition.

notes: STUB. Ancient Hebrew (ISO 639-3 hbo) is the umbrella code for pre-Modern varieties of Hebrew: Biblical/Classical Hebrew (the language of the Hebrew Bible, ~10th c. BCE - 2nd c. CE) and Mishnaic Hebrew. The Masoretic Text's TIBERIAN VOCALIZATION (~10th c. CE) is the best-attested phonological witness: it marks 22 consonant letters plus a system of vowel points distinguishing (per the secondary literature surveyed this session) seven vowel qualities with length and quality contrasts collapsed in Modern Hebrew (he.json), gemination via dagesh, and cantillation/stress. This is NOT the same phonology as he.json (Modern Israeli Hebrew): Tiberian Hebrew preserves distinctions Modern Hebrew merged (e.g. begadkefat spirantisation on all six stops rather than three, pharyngeals ħ/ʕ kept distinct from χ/ʔ, vowel quantity). Building an honest Tiberian grapheme table requires reconciling the Masoretic pointing conventions against a specific scholarly reconstruction (e.g. Khan's 'The Tiberian Pronunciation Tradition of Biblical Hebrew'), which was not fetched with sufficient confidence this session to assert a cited letter-by-letter mapping distinct from he.json's Modern-Hebrew niqqud table; rather than copy he.json's Modern values under a false Ancient-Hebrew label (they encode different, later mergers), this spec is left as a metadata-only stub per the 'never fabricate' rule. graphemes is intentionally empty pending a dedicated Tiberian-reconstruction pass.
